cuts.text: if (r.kind === "labels" && r.reason.trim() === "") out.push(`block ${b.id}: labels rendering needs a reason`);

diverged.why: `RealiseResult`'s false arm carried `reason: string` and now carries a classified `Mismatch` of four kinds; `mismatch(reason)` is deleted so no site can stay unclassified, and `Selection`, `Backend`, the four constructors and `describeMismatch` are new. Spec 1.3 and docs/known-gaps.md G84/G94.

`selectRenderer` is new (spec 1.3's rules: a template that applied and failed refuses, and only an auto block whose every template reported not-applicable reaches ELK); `realiseBlock` is rewired around it, takes an ELK backend, checks the layout whoever drew it, and turns a template's thrown error into a `backend-raised` mismatch instead of rethrowing.
`TraceResult`'s false arm carries a `Mismatch`; all eight of its refusals are shape tests over the subgraph and are `not-applicable`.

`Measured`'s false arm carries a `Mismatch`, forwarded from `tryPlaceFields` rather than rebuilt from its string, so the `clearance` classification survives the two templates that measure their own drawing.

`FieldsResult`'s false arm carries a `clearance` Mismatch, which needs two things the ported code did not keep: the obstacle that blocks the preferred slot (`clear` became `blockerOf`) and the block's id (`FieldScene.scope` became `FieldScene.block`, with the prose derived from it so every message is unchanged). `blockFieldsResult` is new, for the caller that forwards the mismatch.
Five refusal sites classified, all `not-applicable`, and `CommonRailLadder` carries a `Mismatch`.
Six refusal sites classified, all `not-applicable`.
One refusal site, a forward; `Classified` carries a `Mismatch` and every `classifyChain` refusal is `not-applicable`.
Six refusal sites classified: five `not-applicable` shape tests and one forward of the field-placement `clearance` measurement.

Eight refusal sites classified, and the only two `invalid-geometry` sites in the template set are here: a bus-net pin on the wrong side of the symbol, and a tied pin whose end is not in the bus column. Each names the IR connection it failed to realise. `Banks` and `reachOf`'s result carry a `Mismatch`.
`Planned` and the local `Core` carry a `Mismatch`; every `planStage` refusal is `not-applicable`, and the one reason it rephrases keeps the kind by spreading the mismatch rather than rebuilding it.
One refusal site, a forward of `planStage`'s mismatch.

Three refusal sites classified, and the third is the only `clearance` site in the template set: it has drawn all four rotations and `checkLayout` refused every one, so it names the constraint and the obstacle pair of rotation 0's first problem (render/problem-obstacles.ts) and refuses rather than guessing a pair it cannot recover.

Twelve assertions compared a `classifyChain` refusal against `{ ok: false, reason }`. They now assert the KIND as well, which is stronger, not weaker - a site that silently became `invalid-geometry` would fail. This is ruling R4's one permitted edit to a ported test's assertions: the widening requires it, and it is declared here rather than smuggled in.

Plan decision D3: `Rendering` loses `{ kind: "labels"; reason }` and gains `{ kind: "auto" }`. The pedals source has `labels` and keeps it, so no rewrite rule reconciles the two. The MCU `cuts` this entry carried in files[] (G112: PinmapInput, CircuitSpec.mcu, Circuit.mcu, the "pinmap" pin origin) were applied before it diverged and the file on disk is that cut form; they are no longer declared anywhere but the git history of this manifest.

D3: `labelledNets` tested `rendering.kind !== "wired"`, which with `auto` added would label every net of an ELK-rendered block. It now means not `wired` and not `auto`, i.e. `bus` - a modification, which a cut cannot express.

D3: `BlockReport.rendering` was "wired" | "bus" | "labels" and the switch over `Rendering` had a `case "labels"` returning its reason. With `labels` deleted and `auto` added, the case is uninhabited and the switch is no longer exhaustive.

D3: the SPLIT and PEER blocks and `labelsCircuit`'s block B declared `{ kind: "labels" }`. They are `{ kind: "bus", groups: [] }` here, which `labelledNets` and `valuesAlong` treat identically (every net labelled, values along their glyphs), so every fixture-backed assertion measures what it did. Its MCU `cuts` (G112) were applied before divergence.

D3: three block specs declared `{ kind: "labels" }`, now `{ kind: "bus", groups: [] }`. Its nine MCU `cuts` (G112) were applied before divergence and are no longer declared anywhere but this manifest's history.

D3: two block specs declared `{ kind: "labels" }` and one test was named for it. They are `{ kind: "bus", groups: [] }` and the test is renamed; the ASSERTION is unchanged, because `bus` is the non-wired kind whose nets are all labelled now that `auto`'s are not. Its MCU `cuts` (G112) were applied before divergence.

D3: the shared `LABELS` rendering is `{ kind: "bus", groups: [] }`, and the V6 test "requires a reason for label rendering" is DELETED with the rule it tested (supersede means delete; the cut that removes that rule from ir/validate.ts is declared in files[]). Its MCU `cuts` (G112) were applied before divergence.
D3: one block spec declared `{ kind: "labels" }`, now `{ kind: "bus", groups: [] }`.
D3: one `blockCircuit` rendering argument declared `{ kind: "labels" }`, now `{ kind: "bus", groups: [] }`.
